title: The Mechanical Witness
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0876.txt (342 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Detective-cast (Conan, Kogoro Mouri) omitted by convention. case_type: murder (functionally manslaughter -- the culprit caused the victim's death while fleeing after being caught mid-theft, not via a deliberate strangling). Corrections vs. the old low-fidelity case file: (1) the old file's object 'Rope, worn from repeated use on a gas pipe' reversed the physical clue -- the transcript is explicit that the GAS PIPE (the rope's interior anchor point) was worn from repeated use and broke under strain during the struggle, nearly dropping Isshiki; the rope itself stayed intact and only became lethal when Tanizaki grabbed it to try to save Isshiki and it tangled around his own neck. (2) the old file's has_motive_against edge pointed Isshiki's financial motive at the victim Tanizaki personally; the transcript shows Isshiki's theft-for-profit motive was against the company/president (Kusumi), and Tanizaki's death was incidental to intercepting the theft, not the target of any grudge. (3) added fidelity the old file omitted entirely: the climax's two on-screen red-herring accusations (against Horiuchi for personal dislike, against Kusumi for believing Tanizaki was the leak), plus the parallel red-herring pair of wrongly-suspected outsider Makita (Myojo Technics, general affairs, alibied) vs. the actual recipient of the stolen tech, Hiraguchi (Myojo Technics R&D). The old file's stated culprit (Isshiki Kazuomi) is otherwise confirmed correct by the transcript.

clues.desc: The robot's sensor flags the same rare trap ink on Isshiki's shoe/toe that it was built to detect on the thief -- ink Isshiki claims he merely 'has at home,' but which is exclusive to Tanizaki's trap.

Footprints on the office floor, rust marks matching both the water heater and Tanizaki's back, and blood on the ventilation fan together prove Tanizaki was hoisted by the rope at the broken gas-pipe/fan gap rather than simply overcome by gas.
Makita (Myojo Technics general affairs, alibied) was first suspected as Tanizaki's outside contact, but the real recipient of the leaked technology was Hiraguchi of Myojo's R&D department.
